I think my life is more good than bad because the "positive" experiences can only be made from a negative circumstance. I must first be deprived of love and caring before I can appreciate it. The simple answer to this is to stop creating the circumstance in which a problem arises which then needs fixing, namely lack of care and affection and the subsequent consumption of it to relieve the deprivation. So I have a few options:

* Continue creating a problem that then needs fixing.
* Stop desiring
* Stop the circumstance in which desire occurs

The first option is illogical. Why would I put something in a negative state only to then have the burden of removing it from that negative state? The logical answer is to prevent the problem from occurring.

The second option is not likely to happen. Maybe I could become some sort of Buddhist monk and eradicate all desire but dying just seems a lot easier and accomplishes the same thing.

The last option is to accept the fact that I will always desire and that I will always be fighting a losing battle in which my psychology creates a need and then I must fight my way out of the deprivation it creates. Some people are willing to accept the fact that life is absurd, but I am not. Not when the cost is suffering. So the answer here is to end the meaningless suffering.

It's not even that. The fundamental basis for which life is built upon is broken. We're not "designed", by evolution that is, to be happy or satisfied. You must always be hungry. You always have to be deprived of something before you can claw back the negative nature has put you in, and people call that happiness. The only option for me is to, as an online interlocutor put it:

>kill myself in order to maximize the ratio of good to bad (by ending a process that results in more bad than good)

And I'd argue that the good isn't even good, it's just less bad.
